Project Management Fundamentals and Core: Demonstrate an understanding of the various project life cycles and processes
Demonstrate an understanding of project management planning
Demonstrate an understanding of project roles and responsibilities
Determine how to follow and execute planned strategies or frameworks (e.g., communication, risks, etc.)
Demonstrate an understanding of common problem-solving tools and techniques
Predictive, Plan-Based Methodologies: Explain when it is appropriate to use a predictive, plan-based approach
Demonstrate an understanding of a project management plan schedule
Determine how to document project controls of predictive, plan-based projects
Agile Frameworks/Methodologies: Explain when it is appropriate to use an adaptive approach
Determine how to plan project iterations
Determine how to document project controls for an adaptive project
Explain the components of an adaptive plan
Determine how to prepare and execute task management steps
Business Analysis Frameworks: Demonstrate an understanding of business analysis (BA) roles and responsibilities
Determine how to conduct stakeholder communication
Demonstrate an understanding of product roadmaps
Determine how project methodologies influence business analysis processes

stem_hints: Which technique is used to identify roles and the level of responsibilities?
Which tool can be used to prioritize the requirements?
prompt_template:
@options
Give each question between 4 and 6 options. Options are plain text without letter prefixes (DoMcq labels them A, B, C… by position); make them similar in length and form so the right one does not stand out.
Write the real exam's two kinds of item, as PMI's own CAPM sample questions show them. Most are multiple choice: exactly 4 options and exactly one correct, so `answer` is a single letter. A few are multiple response: 5 or 6 options, two or more of them correct and at least one incorrect, and the stem says how many to choose ("Choose TWO.", "Choose THREE."); `answer` lists every correct letter in ascending order ("BD").
Never use these as an option: "all of the above", "none of the above". Avoid "both A and B" style options too.
